learning_outcomes.text: Provide the student with the fundamentals of Electrical Engineering.
Discuss basic concepts and methodology in the field of stationary and slow varying electromagnetism.
Treat in detail subjects concerning circuit analysis in D.C. and A.C. regime.
Discuss the basic theory for electromechanical devices.
Treat the basic theory of electric power systems.

syllabus_topics: Circuit Theory: Kirchhoff's Laws.
Circuit Elements and their characteristics, resistor, capacitor, inductor, dependent and independent voltage and current sources, ideal transformer.
Graph of a circuit, tree and co-tree, sets of fundamental cuts and fundamental loops.
DC regime.
Circuit Analysis Methods.
Main theorems on linear network.
Transient analysis.
AC regime: Stainmetz transform, AC circuit analysis methods, AC power.
Three-Phase Systems.
Electric Power Systems: Generation and transmission.
Safety basic concepts.
Electromagnetism: definitions and Maxwell equations in integral form.
From fields theory to circuit theory.
Magnetic circuits.
Power losses in electric machines.
Transformer. Basic principle. Internal and external equations. Equivalent circuits. Open circuit and short circuit test, efficiency measurements.
Three-Phase transformer.
Rotating field theory.
Induction machine. Basic principle. Internal and external equations. Equivalence theorem for asynchronous machines. Equivalent circuit. Torque-speed and current-speed characteristics.
Synchronous-speed machine. Basic principle. Internal and external equations.
D.C. machines. Basic principle. Internal and external equations.
Equivalent circuits. Torque-speed and current-speed characteristics.

assessment_methods.method: Take-home written paper on a topic relevant to the program (electrical machines with an application example and circuit calculation)

assessment_rules: The take-home written paper lasts 60 minutes and its maximum length is 4 sides. The choice of topic is at the student's discretion but must concern electrical machines and include an application example with relative circuit calculation. The evaluation considers relevance, clarity of presentation, correct use of terminology, presence of a numerical example, and citation of sources. Results are published on Almaesami within approximately two weeks and remain valid for one year, unless replaced by a subsequent result.
bibliography: G. Rizzoni, “Principles and applications of electrical engineering”, McGrow-Hill, 2015.
institution: Università Di Bologna - Alma Mater Studiorum
